messages:
carol: Quick heads up — planning to publish Py + TS SDKs tomorrow during the 08:00 PST change window. Need to confirm lockfile pin, npm dist-tag, and the deprecation blurb for sync client.

dane: Ack. Are we still doing staggered cohorts or full rollout? :eyes:

carol: Staggered. 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 2 hours if no errors. Rollback plan ready.

emma: I can draft the deprecation note for sync client. Do we want to suggest migration code snippets? probably short examples only.

frank: I will handle wheel building + twine upload. Reminder: ephemeral token expires at 07:45 PST, so i'll rotate now and post creds to the publish bot.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Release checklist created: SDK Publish (py/ts) — run `./scripts/release-checklist.sh` and mark steps. Status: pending.

carol: @emma include guidance to use the async client and link to migration gist. Keep the note neutral — warn about removed sync APIs in next major.

emma: Draft ready, putting in /docs/releases/drafts. Short blurb + example for await client.start().

dane: For npm: we should publish under `next` dist-tag first. Command I usually run:
```
npm publish --tag next --access public
npm dist-tag add my-sdk@1.3.0 next
```
Confirm that we set `latest` only after 100% rollout.

frank: Py steps:
```
python -m build
twine upload dist/* --repository pypi
```
I'll hold the final twine push until canary passes.

carol: Lockfile pinning — ops wants us to pin the `platform-client` transitive dep to 2.1.x for this release. Who can add to the lockfile and open PR?

frank: I can update poetry lock and push a PR to `release/py-ts-1.3.0`. Will include a note in the PR body: "Pin platform-client to 2.1.x (regressions observed in 2.2.x)".

dane: I will kick off the canary cohort after lockfile PR merges. If any test fails, we revert the dist-tag and yank the wheel.

devex-release: @channel Publish runbook: 1) merge lockfile PR 2) run `./scripts/release-checklist.sh` 3) publish under `next`/canary 4) verify smoke tests (<10m) 5) promote dist-tags 6) publish release notes 7) mark deprecation notice in docs. Link: https://go/release-runbook/sdk

emma: One more ask — we should call out the deprecation on the release notes and in the console banner. Can someone add the console PR?

carol: @frank can you open the console banner PR after docs are up? also, ensure release notes include migration snippet + link to migration gist.

frank: will do. opening PR now.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Canary cohort publish started for @dane — npm tag `next` pushed, wheel uploaded to pypi-test (staged). Check build logs: https://ci/reports/2734567890

dane: Canary smoke: generation tests + auth flow ok so far. latency spike at step 3 was transient.

emma: landing the deprecation blurb in the release notes PR now.

carol: If canary remains green for 30m, promote to 50% then monitor. If any consumer errors appear, revert dist-tag and yank package, and post here.

frank: 30m green. promoting to 50%.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Promotion complete: cohort=50% -- monitoring enabled.

dane: seeing an uptick in tokenization errors from one integration test run — digging in. tagging @frank.

frank: found culprit: an optional kw param changed in platform-client 2.2.x; our pin prevented that but one integration slipped to 2.2 in staging. Rolling that instance back to 2.1.3 now.

carol: Good catch. Once fixed, continue to 100%. If rollback takes >15m, stop rollout and yank.

dane: rollback done. tests passing. proceed to 100%.

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Promotion complete: cohort=100% — publish marked as successful. Release notes: https://go/releases/sdk-1.3.0

emma: Release notes and deprecation blurb published. Console banner PR up: #4567

carol: Closing notes: - confirm phone home telemetry looks normal - add follow-up on migration metrics in next week's retro. Thanks everyone :pulse:

frank: will tag post-release ticket and pin lockfile commit. :shipit:

deploy-bot: [deploy-bot] Post-release automation: changelog attached, metrics job scheduled for +24h.

carol: Thread closed unless new issues surface.
